# Radio

Radio — single option within a named radio group. Supports controlled (`isChecked`) and uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`) usage. Built on Base UI's Radio, wrapped in `FieldFrame` (A7) for the label and the description caption. Base UI's Radio has no standalone `checked` prop — selection lives on a `RadioGroup` ancestor. `RadioGroup` renders one real, shared Base UI `RadioGroup` around all of its options and passes each one `grouped`, so the group gets Base UI's native roving-tabindex keyboard nav across options for free, same as `ChoiceGrid`'s radio-type rows. A `Radio` used on its own (no `grouped`, the default) — a lone question, a `ChoiceGrid` cell, or sibling Radios sharing a bare `name` the way the "Group" story composes them — owns a private, single-item group instead, so it stays independently controllable exactly like the native input it replaces. That private group keeps its own `role="radiogroup"` (axe rejects `aria-readonly`/ `aria-required` on a role-less `div`) but drops the `aria-labelledby` it would otherwise inherit from an ambient Fieldset legend it has no business naming itself after.

**Import:** `import { Radio } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use Radio when the options need custom presentation, such as options listed in a table. For a plain list of options, use RadioGroup, which owns the group label, the value and the error.

Make one option the default: the safest and lowest-risk one. If a person may decline all options, add a "None" option; if the list cannot be complete, add "Other".

## Best practices

### Show one answer selected at a time. {#show-one-answer-selected-at-a-time}

A radio group holds exactly one answer. Never show two selected.

Do: One radio selected in the group.
Don't: Two radios selected at once.

### Never preselect a high-risk answer. {#never-preselect-a-high-risk-answer}

Leave consequential choices, such as ones about privacy or payment, for the
person to make on purpose. When an option starts selected, make it the safe
one.

Do: The safe option, Keep my history, starts selected.
Don't: The high-risk option, Delete my history, starts selected.

### Keep labels short and parallel. {#keep-labels-short-and-parallel}

Short labels scan as a list; long ones wrap and blur the choices.

Do: Short, parallel labels.
Don't: Long labels that wrap, beside a one-word one.

### Order options by likelihood or risk. {#order-options-by-likelihood-or-risk}

Do: Order options from most to least likely, or from least to most risk.
Don't: Alphabetical order cannot be localized and says nothing about which option fits most people.

### A lone Radio is not a group. {#a-lone-radio-is-not-a-group}

Radios that share a `name` are one group; each option gets its own id. ARIA allows `aria-readonly` on a radiogroup and not on a radio, so a read-only question belongs in RadioGroup, which announces it.

### Avoid long lists and overlapping ranges. {#avoid-long-lists-and-overlapping-ranges}

For a long list, use Select. Do not write numeric options that overlap ("0-20", "20-40") or skip a number.

### A description describes; the label names. {#a-description-describes-the-label-names}

`description` renders under the label and is read after the name.

## Accessibility

- **Each option has its own id.** The component derives one per instance, so labels never resolve to the first radio of the group.
- **A radio with no `label` has no accessible name.** Pass `aria-label` where the design has no room for visible text.
- **Include an error message for a required or invalid group**, for example "Select an option".
- **Disable an option only for something the person can fix on the same screen.** Put the reason in the option's `description`, at full contrast, and never in a tooltip. A disabled option leaves the tab order. For a choice that must stay reachable, keep it enabled and use validation, so a screen reader user hears why it cannot be chosen.
- **Keyboard focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the radio.** Arrow keys move between the radios of a group.

## Related

- For several answers from a list, use Checkbox.
- For a longer list of options, use Select.
- To turn something on or off, use Toggle.
- For a whole group with its label, value and error, use RadioGroup.

## Parts

1. **Radio.** A 12 circle. Selected, it fills with the selected bold fill and draws an inverse dot; unselected, it is an empty circle.
2. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the radio in a 24 row. It names the option. A required marker follows it.
3. **Description.** Optional 12/16 text under the label that describes the option. It does not name it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | Unselected: `--ds-background-input-hovered` with a `--ds-border-brand` edge. Selected: the hovered step of the selected bold fill. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered look holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the radio, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill and `--ds-border-selected` edge; the dot is `--ds-icon-inverse`. |
| Invalid | The unselected radio takes `--ds-border-danger`. A selected radio keeps its fill. |
| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, no hover; an unchecked radio takes the `--ds-background-neutral` fill. Not changeable. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill, `--ds-border-disabled` edge, `--ds-icon-disabled` dot. Out of the tab order. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Circle fill and edge | `--ds-background-input` and `--ds-border-input`; selected `--ds-background-selected-bold` and `--ds-border-selected`. |
| Circle size, edge width | `--radio-control-size` (12); `--stroke-2`. |
| Row | `--item-height-sm` (24); gap `--space-050`. |
| Label | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Card | `--radius-025`, `--stroke-1` edge in `--ds-border`, `--ds-surface` fill. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write each label as the option: "In person". | A sentence or an instruction: "Choose this if you meet in person." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Keep labels parallel in length and form. | Mix one word with a full clause. |
| Add "None" when a person may decline every option, "Other" when the list cannot be complete. | Force an answer that does not fit. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Select an option". | "Required" or "Invalid". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the radio button, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string (required) | — | Form key of the radio group. Options that belong together share it, and it is reported in `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | — | The text that names this option. |
| `value` | string or number | — | Form value of this option, and the `target.value` that `onChange` reports when it is chosen. |
| `isChecked` | bool | — | Controlled selected state. Pair it with `onChange`; when it is set, `defaultChecked` is ignored. |
| `defaultChecked` | bool | — | Whether an uncontrolled radio starts selected. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error state, for an option that fails validation. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction and dims this option. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the option without letting the user change it. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Shows an asterisk on the label and sets the native `required` attribute. |
| `description` | node | — | Secondary text under the label. It describes the option; it does not name it. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'plain'` | `plain` (default) is a radio beside its label; `card` draws the option as a bordered tile. |
| `grouped` | bool | `false` | Set by `RadioGroup`. Not for direct use. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with `{ target: { name, value, checked: true } }` when the option is chosen. A radio never reports being unchecked. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the radio gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the radio loses focus. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event on the radio button. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `plain` · `card`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
